{{Short description|Company}} {{Use British English|date=February 2020}} {{Infobox company | name = Senoko Energy | logo = File:Logo for Senoko Energy Wikipedia Article.png | type = [[Privately held company|Private]] | industry = [[Electric utility]] | fate = | predecessor = | successor = | founded = {{Start date and age|1977}} | hq_location_city = | hq_location_country = [[Singapore]] | area_served = | key_people = Graeme York
(President and [[CEO]]) | products = | parent = Lion Power | website = {{URL|https://www.senokoenergy.com}} }} '''Senoko Energy''' is one of Singapore's largest power generation companies in Singapore, accounting for approximately 20% of the nation's electricity supply. ==History== Senoko Power was originally formed in 1977{{cite news | last=Tang| first=See Kit| title =Senoko Energy clarifies that it does not need more Government funding in 'foreseeable future'| publisher=CNA| date =19 November 2019 | url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/senoko-energy-clarifies-does-not-need-more-government-funding-12106380| access-date =6 February 2020}} as a power generation arm of the [[Public Utilities Board (Singapore)|Public Utilities Board]] (PUB) in Singapore.{{cite book |last=Tan |first=Chwee Huat |date=1 June 2002 |title=Singapore Financial & Business Sourcebook |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KV72O4mQ-WwC&dq=%22power+senoko%22+%22public+utilities+board%22&pg=PA662 |location=Singapore |publisher=University of Singapore Press |pages=623, 662 |isbn=978-9971692568 }} In the 1990s, it converted the Power Station from an open-cycle [[gas turbine power plant]] to Singapore's first [[combined cycle power plant|combined cycle plant]].{{cite news | title =Environmental innovations seen in 1997 Project of the Year winners| magazine=Power Engineering International| date =1 November 1997 | url =https://www.powerengineeringint.com/1997/11/01/environmental-innovations-seen-in-1997-project-of-the-year-winners/| access-date =6 February 2020}} It also began piping in natural gas from Malaysia to generate electricity in 1992.{{cite book |last=Hoong Ng |first=Weng |date=28 November 2011 |title=Singapore, the Energy Economy: From The First Refinery To The End Of Cheap Oil, 1960-2010 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bc21Qxwn9r8C&dq=%22senoko+power%22+%22temasek%22&pg=PA117 |publisher=Routledge |pages=116–117, 121, 131 |isbn=978-0415686754 }} In October 1995, the electricity and gas departments of the PUB corporatised their holdings and vested the electricity and gas undertakings under the [[Government of Singapore|Singapore government]]'s investment arm, [[Temasek Holdings]]. Within Temasek Holdings, the newly formed [[Singapore Power]] was structured as a holding company for five separate subsidiaries, including PowerSenoko Limited (the original corporate name for the company that would become Senoko Energy). [[File:Senoko Power Station located on the northern coast of Singapore.jpg|thumb|Senoko Power Station located on the northern coast of Singapore]] In April 2001, Singapore Power's power generation subsidiaries (including PowerSenoko) were fully divested to Temasek. That same month, a new statutory body, the [[Energy Market Authority]] (EMA), was established.{{cite book |last1=Barton |first1=Barry |last2=Redgwell |first2=Catherine |last3=Rønne |first3=Anita |last4=Zillman |first4=Donald N. |date=3 June 2004 |title=Energy Security: Managing Risk in a Dynamic Legal and Regulatory Environment |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ZKsTFgArP50C&dq=%22energy+market+authority%22&pg=PA403 |location=Oxford, England |publisher=Oxford University Press |pages=403–404 |isbn=978-0199271610 }}{{cite news | title =China Huaneng to pay $3.1b for Tuas Power| newspaper=China Daily| date =14 March 2008 | url =http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/business/2008-03/14/content_6537573.htm| access-date =9 February 2020}}{{cite journal |last1=Low |first1=Linda| date=2002 |title=Rethinking Singapore Inc. and GLCs |journal=Southeast Asian Affairs |volume= 2002|pages=282–302 |jstor=27913213}} PowerSenoko was renamed Senoko Power Limited{{cite news | title =Senoko to add to its Singapore Electricity Market| magazine=Power Engineering| date =13 October 2003 | url =https://www.power-eng.com/2003/10/13/senoko-to-add-to-its-singapore-electricity-market/| access-date =9 February 2020}} and it was among the first three companies to receive a power trading licence from the EMA.{{cite news | title =Three generators to dominate Singapore power market|magazine=Power Engineering International| date =9 July 2002 | url =https://www.powerengineeringint.com/2002/07/09/three-generators-to-dominate-singapore-power-market/| access-date =9 February 2020}} In April 2004, the company began a $50-million ([[Singaporean dollar|SGD]]) power plant upgrade, which eventually made it the largest electricity producer in Singapore.{{cite news | title =Senoko sets aside S$50mil for power plant upgrade| newspaper=The Star | date =1 April 2004 | url =https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2004/04/01/senoko-sets-aside-s50mil-for-power-plant-upgrade| access-date =13 February 2020}}{{cite news | last1=Guerrera| first1=Francisco| last2=Burtonin| first2=John| title =Temasek 'preparing for' electricity sale| newspaper=Financial Times| date =6 October 2005 | url =https://www.ft.com/content/5749bc28-3686-11da-bedc-00000e2511c8| access-date =13 February 2020}} In September 2008, a consortium led by Japanese trading company, [[Marubeni]], acquired Senoko Power from Temasek Holdings for $3.65 billion (SGD). Other members of the consortium included [[Kyushu Electric Power]], [[Kansai Electric Power Company|Kansai Electric]], the Japan Bank of International Cooperation, and GDF Suez (now [[Engie]]) of [[France]].{{cite news | title =Consortium led by Marubeni to buy Senoko Power of Singapore| newspaper=The New York Times| date =5 September 2008 | url =https://www.nytimes.com/2008/09/05/business/worldbusiness/05iht-power.1.15921241.html| access-date =9 February 2020}} The consortium is known as Lion Power Holdings with Marubeni and Engie holding the most shares at 30% each. Also in 2008, the company started converting three of its oil-fired turbines (producing 750 [[Megawatt|MW]] of power) into two natural gas-fired turbines (producing 862 MW of power).{{cite news | last=Chua| first=Grace| title =Senoko Energy producing electricity using less fuel| newspaper=Straits Times| date =6 February 2013 | url =https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/senoko-energy-producing-electricity-using-less-fuel| access-date =14 February 2020}} The $1-billion (SGD) repowering project was completed in 2013 and resulted in a 1-million ton reduction in carbon dioxide emissions annually.{{cite news | title =Senoko Energy repowers generating stations in Singapore| work=Power Technology | date =7 February 2013 | url =https://www.power-technology.com/uncategorised/newssenoko-energy-repowers-generating-stations-in-singapore/| access-date =14 February 2020}} In 2010, the company underwent restructuring and became known by its current name, Senoko Energy Private Limited.{{cite news | last=Chua| first=Tony| title =Boustead subsidiary to construct water treatment plant | work=Singapore Business Review | date =8 October 2010 | url =https://sbr.com.sg/building-engineering/news/boustead-subsidiary-construct-water-treatment-plant| access-date =14 February 2020}}{{cite news | last=Thien| first=Rachel| title =Brunei princess tours Singapore's biggest energy provider| work=AsiaOne | date =5 November 2011 | url =https://www.asiaone.com/News/AsiaOne%2BNews/Singapore/Story/A1Story20111105-308912.html| access-date =14 February 2020}} In November 2016, the company became one of the founding members of the Singapore chapter of the [[World Energy Council]].{{cite news | last=Soh| first=Andrea| title =Singapore power companies form local chapter of World Energy Council| newspaper=Business Times| date =10 November 2016 | url =https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/energy-commodities/singapore-power-companies-form-local-chapter-of-world-energy-council| access-date =14 February 2020}} In April 2018, Senoko Energy began offering consumers individual energy plans for households and [[small and medium-sized enterprises]] as part of the EMA's soft launch of the Open Electricity Market in Singapore.{{cite news | last=Mui| first=Rachel| title =Senoko Energy launches retail services for consumers ahead of market liberalisation| newspaper=Straits Times | date =7 March 2018 | url =https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/senoko-energy-launches-retail-services-for-consumers-ahead-of-market| access-date =14 February 2020}} It was one of 13 approved electricity retailers when the Open Electricity Market opened nationwide{{cite news | last=Tang| first=See Kit| title =Full opening of electricity market in Singapore to fire up competition: What will retailers do?| publisher=CNA | date =1 October 2018 | url =https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/full-opening-of-electricity-market-in-singapore-to-fire-up-10767418| access-date =13 February 2020}} in May 2019.{{cite news | title =5 myths about the Open Electricity Market| newspaper=The Straits Times| date =4 May 2019 | url =https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/5-myths-about-the-open-electricity-market| access-date =14 February 2020}} It was one of six that also generated its own power.{{cite news | last=Gabriel| first=Anita| title =Power grab in Singapore's electricity market could spur consolidation| newspaper=Business Times| date =4 March 2019 | url =https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/energy-commodities/power-grab-in-singapores-electricity-market-could-spur-consolidation-0| access-date =14 February 2020}} In November 2024, [[Sembcorp]] Industries, through its subsidiary Sembcorp Utilities, acquired Engie’s 30% stake in Senoko Energy, increasing its shareholding in the company.{{Cite web |title=SEMBCORP INDUSTRIES LTD : 15-Nov-2024 |url=https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/N1QDC5HIP69K1AO9/ |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=links.sgx.com}} In June 2025, Sembcorp Utilities and Marubeni Corporation increased their interest in Senoko Energy to 50% each by acquiring the shares of KPIC Netherlands, Kyuden International, and the Japan Bank of International Cooperation. This established a 50/50 joint ownership structure between Sembcorp and Marubeni. Marubeni stated it intended to strengthen Senoko’s profitability, competitiveness, and corporate value in partnership with Sembcorp, while ensuring a stable electricity supply for Singapore.{{Cite web |title=SEMBCORP INDUSTRIES LTD : 13-Jun-2025 |url=https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/LW55D5JPHQD3LN7I/f497ab01df15c8899afc9e32881f2c4afea31b46caf43d817f26a7a406ed1ccc |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=links.sgx.com}}{{Cite web |last=Marubeni Corporation |title=Additional Investment in Senoko Energy Pte. Ltd. in Singapore |url=https://www.marubeni.com/en/news/2025/release/00025.html |website=Marubeni Corporation}} ==Subsidiaries== Senoko Energy has three subsidiaries: Senoko Energy Supply, Senoko Services, and Senoko Gas Supply. Senoko Energy Supply is the company's retail arm that sells electricity and other services to consumers in Singapore. Senoko Services leases out fuel storage tanks and provides terminal services. Senoko Gas Supply is a licensed gas shipper and retailer that is authorised by the EMA to ship gas throughout the country's gas network.{{cite news | title =S'pore gas retailers cleared to go islandwide| newspaper=Business Times| date =21 June 2014 | url =https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/top-stories/spore-gas-retailers-cleared-to-go-islandwide| access-date =14 February 2020}}{{cite news | title =Gas Shipper| publisher=Energy Market Authority| url =https://www.ema.gov.sg/Licensees_Gas_Shipper.aspx| access-date =14 February 2020}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.senokoenergy.com Official website] [[Category:Energy companies of Singapore]] [[Category:Energy companies established in 1977]] [[Category:Singaporean companies established in 1977]]
